newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals rise on yen's weaker tone.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals rise on yen's weaker tone.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly higher on Wednesday, backed by stronger spot prices and the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from six yen to 15 yen per gram firmer. Benchmark April was up eight yen at 1,243 yen.

Volume in gold futures was buoyant in line with the volatile currency market. "We were struggling to catch up with the volatile currency market, which lifted volume in gold futures. But trade was directionless, with active two-way trade detected," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $342.60/343.10 per ounce at 0753 GMT, against $342.70/343.20 in New York on Tuesday.
Although the U.S. decision to keep interest rates unchanged provided support in New York on Tuesday, it was not enough to boost prices during Asian trading hours, traders said.
In the local bullion market, traders said Japanese gold investment demand has recovered in May as the yen's strength has pushed down yen-based retail prices.
For platinum group metals, news that Russian PGM exports will resume soon has been digested by the platinum and palladium futures market, traders said.

Traders were relieved that the long-awaited Japan-Russia PGM 1997 contract talks have been set to take place in early June. But they were concerned over the possibility that high palladium prices could dent domestic demand. "When the palladium market is back to normal, chances are high that Japan's palladium demand will fall sharply," one trader said.
Platinum futures ranged from 15 yen to 39 yen per gram firmer. Benchmark April platinum was 17 yen higher at 1,365.
Benchmark April palladium was up eight yen at 607 yen. Benchmark April silver was up 1.4 yen per 10 grams at 173.9 yen. --Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
